title: Protesters clash with police in Paris over living costs
seoTitle: Paris cost of living protests and clashes

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated over rising living costs, declining purchasing power, public services, economic hardship, and inequality.
tea.want: Protesters demanded better living conditions, economic relief, and addressed concerns regarding school conditions and public services.
tea.changed: Oct 18: Authorities reported widespread arrests and clashes following demonstrations across multiple cities.

summary: Mass demonstrations and protests over rising living costs, declining purchasing power, and public services took place across France, including Paris. The movement initially grew out of weeks of student protests concerning school conditions and teacher shortages before broadening into nationwide economic demonstrations. In Paris and other cities like Marseille, Bordeaux, and Lille, events escalated into clashes with police, arson, property damage, and looting of commercial stores. Authorities deployed tear gas and water cannons. French President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, warning that those responsible for vandalism and looting would face legal prosecution. The CGT trade union estimated turnout at 800,000, while Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez and French authorities stated approximately 550,000 people participated nationwide.
demands: Resolve school conditions and teacher shortages
response: Police deployed tear gas and water cannons, arresting hundreds of individuals. President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, vandalism, and looting, promising legal consequences.

crowd.text: approximately 550,000 people participated in the protests, according to French authorities
